$comment: D-FFI-LIBRARY-TLS-EXPORT-BINDS-AS-PLAIN-DATA — the ACCEPTING half of the storage-duration agreement rule, and the arm that keeps the refusal from being a blanket. `library_thread_local_refused` names the TLS export from this same image and must be REFUSED; this entry names the ORDINARY export from it and must BIND. ★★★ WHY THE PAIR AND NOT JUST THE REFUSAL: a rule keyed on `this library exports a thread-local` rather than on `THIS NAME is a thread-local` would refuse every import from any image carrying a .tdata section, which is most real libraries — and it would pass the refusal example perfectly. This is the entry that sees that. It reaches the same call site with the same library on `--resolve-library`: the reader classifies both rows, the binder consults the matched one, and the answer for this name is `ordinary`. ★★ IT NEEDS NO HARNESS CAPABILITY. The SUCCESS arm of both runners has staged `prebuiltLibraries` since the BSD-archive entry, so this example is files only. Its sibling refusal is not, and that asymmetry is the finding this lane reports rather than a property of this entry. ⚠ THE TWO RUNNERS DO NOT WITNESS THE SAME THING HERE, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. ✔MEASURED at this tree: the IN-PROCESS runner reports `compiled=x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec,arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec` — both specs built, artifacts produced, nothing spawned — while the CLI entry passes in 0.26 s having compiled NOTHING, because the integrated runner builds only the HOST-RUNNABLE spec and this entry declares none on any host. That asymmetry is a property of the harness, not of this entry; two corpus manifests already carried it before this one. It is recorded HERE rather than left for a reader to discover, because an entry that asserts in one runner and shrugs in the other must not read as if both had checked. ⇒ THE ASSERTION THIS ENTRY MAKES IS THE IN-PROCESS ONE: a compile that must SUCCEED against a TLS-carrying library, on both ELF targets. ⚠ WHY BOTH ARMS ARE BUILD-ONLY (`runOn: []`), and it is a fact about the runners rather than a choice: an exec importing from a DYNAMIC library needs the loader to FIND that library at run time, which on ELF means LD_LIBRARY_PATH or an rpath neither runner sets. `dynlib_resolve_roundtrip` states the same limitation for the same reason and ships three arms shaped exactly like these. What this entry needs from them is a BUILD-time event — the bind either happens or is refused — so compile-only is the full assertion, and the artifact's existence is checked by the runner. ⓘ FOR WHOEVER GIVES THE RUNNERS A LIBRARY-PATH CAPABILITY: turning these into running arms is a strict improvement and the exitCode is already right — the library's `dss_lib_plain_counter` is 11, `fold(11) & 0x7F` is 42. ⚠ NO `optimizedPipelines` ARM, AND THE REASON IS A HARNESS PROPERTY WORTH KNOWING RATHER THAN A CHOICE. ✔MEASURED at this tree by running this entry through the in-process runner: the arm ledger reports `[skipped-by-runOn] ... arm=release ... (compile not attempted: baseline arm did not run)` — an optimized arm is compiled only where its BASELINE arm RUNS, so on a build-only target a declared `release` arm is never built on any host and asserts nothing anywhere. Declaring one here would be an expectation that never fires, which is the defect this corpus refuses in every other shape. ⇒ ANY example whose arms are build-only is structurally unable to carry a release arm; the lane's `long_branch_imm19_escape` entry is where the release pipeline is exercised end to end. ✔MEASURED anyway, so the difference is on the record if the runners ever gain a library-path capability: comparing the shipped CLI's debug and `--config=release` outputs BYTE-wise at this tree, both ELF images differ (9720 vs 9688 bytes on each target, distinct md5s). ⓘ The `release` pipeline emits X_OptFixpointTruncated on this program; it is a warning about the pipeline's own iteration cap, not about this code. Leg-by-leg results are NOT recorded here — whoever runs the legs writes them.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: The SAME TLS-carrying fixture the refusal example resolves against — that is the whole point of this arm. gcc 13.3.0 / GNU ld 2.42, `-shared -fPIC -Os`, stripped; provenance and rebuild commands in tests/ffi/data/libtls.source.c.
